differences.what: The message discloses that directly reproducing the source's original 'think-about-X vs don't-think-about-X' construction as a sanity check already scores 0.75 (vs. the new method's 0.784), i.e. close to the final result. The write-up never reports this reproduction experiment or score; it only reports a different ablation (steering toward the suppression pole, scoring 0.088) as evidence of novelty.

differences.message_quote: confirmed against the white-bear paper's position ablation

rationale: Both documents explicitly name and credit white-bear steering (Raman 2026) as the prior work the method diverges from, and both give the same core novelty argument (removing the named-concept anchor in favor of a concept-free dual-task contrast) backed by the same two knock-down ablations. The message additionally reveals that simply reproducing the source's original contrast scores 0.75 (near the new method's 0.784) and that the server's position semantics were validated against the source's own ablation—material context about the source and the size of the improvement over it that the write-up omits.
